data.hypothesis: Keep the selected parent’s 256-thread CTA and matching 256-source tile, but stage only x, y, z, and mass in a 16-byte record. This reduces shared memory from 7,168 to 4,096 bytes while preserving source order and force arithmetic. The selected parent measured 0.00099616 s; compact tiles measured 0.00089008 s at 128 threads, 0.00092808 s at 160, and 0.00092263 s at 192. Since those results vary with tile size, this experiment tests compact staging at a fixed 256-thread configuration; no speedup is assumed. The catalog reports eight distinct programs and no repeats.

memory_lessons.applicability: Tile-size comparisons do not isolate the effect of compact staging; comparing this 256-thread compact candidate with the 256-thread full-record parent can test that representation change at a fixed CTA size.
memory_lessons.claim: The compact 128-thread program measured 0.00089008 s, while compact 160- and 192-thread programs measured 0.00092808 s and 0.00092263 s. The measurements do not establish a monotonic tile-size trend.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: If this candidate is valid, compare its official result with the 256-thread full-record parent and the compact 128-thread candidate.

data.notes: The candidate uses 4,096 bytes of shared memory, below the selected parent’s successfully measured 7,168-byte allocation. All threads still reach both CTA barriers; source-tail loads, target reads, and output writes remain bounds-guarded. Correctness and performance are left to the official controller protocol.
transformations: Keep block and items_per_block at 256, preserving one target per thread and a matching source-tile width.
Stage only source x, y, z, and mass in a 16-byte SourceParticle record; set shared_memory_bytes to 4,096.
Preserve ascending source interaction order and force arithmetic, partial-tile handling, both CTA barriers, and target/output bounds checks.
